key_insight: Micropillar compression shows that in anorthite, mechanical twinning is easier than slip, with twinning CRSS near 300 MPa and slip strength dropping strongly as temperature rises.
engineering_relevance: These measurements help constrain crustal rheology models by providing quantitative, temperature-dependent plasticity parameters for a major rock-forming mineral.
method: Focused-ion-beam milled ~1 μm micropillars from three crystal orientations of anorthite single crystals.
Compressed 36 pillars inside an SEM at 25, 300, and 800 °C under ~0.001 s⁻¹ strain rate.
Compared activation of twinning and multiple slip systems from observed pillar deformation responses.
evidence_signal: The study reports deformation data from 36 micropillar tests, showing a temperature-insensitive twinning CRSS around 300 MPa and a marked temperature-dependent reduction in slip yield stress.
watch_item: Micropillar results capture single-crystal, small-scale behavior and may not fully represent polycrystalline crustal deformation where defects, grain interactions, and brittle failure can dominate.
paper_title: Quantification of plastic deformation in anorthite using micropillar compression
